s: The abstract concerns retrieval-augmented generation and introduces Selfmem, a framework that improves generation by iteratively creating and selecting self-generated memory. Selfmem uses a retrieval-augmented generator to produce an unbounded memory pool and a memory selector to choose an output for the next generation round. It is evaluated on neural machine translation, abstractive text summarization, and dialogue generation using fine-tuned small models and few-shot LLMs. The framework achieves state-of-the-art results in four directions on the JRC-Acquis translation dataset, 50.3 ROUGE-1 on XSum, and 62.9 ROUGE-1 on BigPatent.

s: Selfmem is a framework that combines a retrieval-augmented generator with a memory selector to improve generation through iterative memory selection. Its motivation is that model-generated outputs can resemble inference-time data more closely than retrieved training examples, but beam outputs alone provide little information gain. The generator produces candidate pools, while the selector chooses memory using model-free metrics such as BLEU or ROUGE and is trained with a KL-divergence objective. The framework is evaluated on machine translation, summarization, and dialogue generation using seven datasets, including JRC-Acquis, XSum, BigPatent, and DailyDialog.
